why: A home-use taste test of a frozen ready meal with 8,000 customers and 15,000 non-customers is believable, and every rating distribution in the four charts sums to 100%.

Emerging-economy medical equipment spending of $86 billion out of $463 billion worldwide is believable, the running total rises steadily to 100%, and the biggest countries come out at about $21 billion and $13 billion.
Twelve trade magazines earning $1-27 million each, with 5-62 editorial staff and roughly $130,000-$440,000 of revenue per staff member, is believable for a loss-making publisher.
A regional motoring club helping 58,000 drivers a year, 84% of them only once (about 130 one-off drivers a day), with round-the-clock 8-hour shifts is believable.
A $6.1 billion baby food maker eyeing 50 countries worth $47 billion in 10 years is believable, and the cumulative curve puts the biggest two at about $9 billion and $7 billion.
Household incomes of about $2,400-$14,400 at market rates and higher at PPP rates (PPP rates below market rates) are typical of developing nations.
Crop contributions of 0.4-1.2 percentage points to annual harvest value growth are believable, and each crop's land and yield parts add to its stated total.
Wholesale and café profits add to each year's stated total, and margins of 4-5% imply sales of $500-800 million, which is believable for a coffee roaster with its own cafés.
Household incomes of about $2,000-$12,500 at market rates and $5,000-$34,000 at PPP rates are believable for four appliance export markets.

Half-year cinema spend of $11-54 per film club subscriber across quintiles, falling as streaming grows, is believable; quintile 1 spending slightly more than quintile 2 can come from snacks and is not impossible.
